recommendation: Keep the external-repo audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-26900; future OO Incubator changes should preserve the split where patient searches only Patient and subject searches all allowed DeviceUsage.subject targets.
issue_request: FHIR-26900 was a Published/Persuasive OO technical correction for R4 asking that the DeviceUseStatement clinical-patient search parameter restrict DeviceUseStatement.subject to Patient only, rather than allowing Group through the patient parameter.
initial_application: The R4B application commit b717783b86bab2bb3aa9ca289f2cd11a7ba18107 changed source/deviceusestatement/bundle-DeviceUseStatement-search-params.xml from DeviceUseStatement.subject to DeviceUseStatement.subject.where(resolve() is Patient). That commit is on the R4B lineage, not the current core branch; the current branch later renamed the artifact to DeviceUsage and restored the Patient-only expression through the FHIR-41413 family-care work.
additional_context: DeviceUsage is no longer in the active FHIR core build: source/fhir.ini omits it from the current draft-resource/resource metadata, and commit 3b38b80cf23f9cbb306fab8fcedb293315478c32 removed DeviceUsage from core lists while changing core narrative links to the HL7 OO Incubator IG. Related FHIR-28219 and FHIR-32876 confirm the broader clinical-patient target intent, while FHIR-41413 later allowed Group on DeviceUsage.subject but explicitly kept DeviceUsage-patient as DeviceUsage.subject.where(resolve() is Patient) with target Patient.
reconciliation: No FHIR core source was changed. The remaining source/deviceusage files in the core checkout are out-of-build, and the current HL7/oo-incubator source and CI build already define DeviceUsage-patient with expression DeviceUsage.subject.where(resolve() is Patient) and target Patient.

related_jiras.note: Published FHIR-I issue requiring common patient search parameters to use where(resolve() is Patient) and target only Patient when the underlying element is subject.
Published FHIR-I issue about generated clinical-patient targets being broader than Patient, citing DeviceUsage.subject as part of the problem.
Applied R6 OO family-care change allowed Group on DeviceUsage.subject while retaining DeviceUsage-patient as Patient-only and adding a separate subject search parameter.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive correction requiring the DeviceUseStatement patient search parameter to restrict subject to Patient only.

evidence_items.learned: This explains the historical rename and the transition context around the patient/subject split.
